content.text: Stripe’s country restrictions lock out digital creators in Nigeria, Ghana, and other regions. This isn’t a policy oversight—it’s a structural exclusion. PayPal, Gumroad, [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/lemon-squeezy-alternatives-restricted-countries-explained-digital-creators-6|COREMERCH guide to lemon]] Squeezy, and Paddle follow suit, leaving creators without [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-broken-here-infrastructure-3|payment]] processing. The problem isn’t just fees or KYC requirements. It’s that these platforms operate as centralized gatekeepers, deciding who participates in global commerce. Sovereign commerce infrastructure solves this by decentralizing the stack. Instead of renting access, you own the [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-11|The Real]]. This post compares conventional platforms to sovereign stacks like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197). We’ll analyze payment speed, ownership, automation, and real costs. The goal is clear: to give you a permanent alternative, not a workaround.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Digital products

Conventional platforms like Stripe and PayPal offer simplicity—until they don’t. They handle payment processing, but their terms of service explicitly exclude entire countries. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy layer on additional features like product hosting and email automation, but they still rely on Stripe or PayPal for payments. This makes them single points of failure. Sovereign commerce infrastructure, like the Edge Commerce Stack, flips this model. It uses GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, and Supabase for order storage. Payments are processed via NOWPayments, which supports 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee. The stack is deployed to your own infrastructure, so no platform can shut you down. You own the code, the data, and the delivery mechanism. This isn’t a workaround—it’s a permanent base-layer solution.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe and PayPal exclude countries based on regulatory risk, not technical limitations. Their compliance teams decide who gets access, and creators in restricted regions are left with no recourse. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy inherit these restrictions because they depend on Stripe or PayPal. Sovereign stacks bypass this entirely. By using NOWPayments for crypto transactions, the Edge Commerce Stack removes centralized gatekeepers. Buyers pay with cryptocurrencies like USDT on BSC, Solana, or TRON—networks with fees under $0.10 per transaction. The stack verifies payments on-chain and delivers products automatically. No KYC, no buyer accounts, no platform approval required. This architecture is pressure-tested in regions like Zimbabwe, where currency collapse and payment rejection are the norm. It’s built for creators who need infrastructure that works regardless of geopolitical risk.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe and PayPal process payments instantly but charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. They also hold funds for days or weeks, especially for accounts in high-risk regions. Crypto payments via NOWPayments confirm in minutes and cost 0.5%. The Edge Commerce Stack integrates this directly into your infrastructure, so there’s no middleman holding your funds. Conventional platforms also charge monthly fees for advanced features. Gumroad’s Pro plan is $10/month, and Lemon Squeezy takes 5% of revenue. Sovereign stacks have no recurring fees. The $197 cost of the Edge Commerce Stack is a one-time payment. You own the deployed infrastructure, so there are no ongoing costs. The real cost of conventional platforms isn’t just fees—it’s the risk of being locked out entirely. Sovereign architecture eliminates that risk.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure removes centralized gatekeepers.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Stripe, PayPal, or their dependents, you rent access to their infrastructure. They own your data, your customer relationships, and your ability to sell. If they shut you down, you lose everything. Sovereign stacks give you full ownership. The Edge Commerce Stack deploys to your GitHub or Cloudflare account, using your Supabase database and Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Automation is handled via Cloudflare Workers, which execute backend logic without servers. When a payment confirms on-chain, the webhook triggers instant product delivery. This isn’t just ownership—it’s control. You decide how your stack evolves, not a platform’s product team. This is infrastructure sovereignty, not a temporary fix.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in a country Stripe supports, conventional platforms might work—for now. But if you’re in Nigeria, Ghana, or another restricted region, they’re not an option. Sovereign commerce infrastructure is the only permanent solution. The Edge Commerce Stack is built for creators who need to sell globally without relying on centralized platforms. It’s not the easiest option—deployment requires technical understanding. But it’s the only option that gives you full ownership and control. If you’re selling digital products and need a stack that works regardless of geopolitical risk, this is your architecture. It’s not a workaround. It’s base-layer infrastructure designed for the people Stripe locked out.

If you’re ready to deploy sovereign commerce infrastructure, the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) gives you a complete solution in 48 hours. It includes Cloudflare Pages hosting, Cloudflare Workers backend, Supabase database, and NOWPayments integration. Five products are loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC is configured, and end-to-end testing ensures everything works. This isn’t a temporary fix—it’s a permanent architecture designed for creators who need to own their infrastructure.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Choose your hosting: GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Both are free and globally distributed. 2. Set up backend logic: Use Cloudflare Workers for serverless execution or Google Apps Script for simplicity. 3. Configure order storage: Supabase provides a scalable database, or use Google Sheets for lighter loads. 4. Deliver files: Upload products to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for instant delivery. 5. Integrate payments: NOWPayments handles crypto transactions with a 0.5% fee and no KYC. 6. Deploy the stack: The Edge Commerce Stack automates this process, ensuring everything works together. 7. Test end-to-end: Verify payment processing, order storage, and file delivery before going live.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use the Edge Commerce Stack if I’m not technical?

The stack is designed for deployment by COREMERCH in 48 hours. After delivery, basic technical understanding is required to manage your infrastructure. If you can follow documentation, you can maintain it.
What cryptocurrencies does NOWPayments support?
NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, and stablecoins on BSC, Solana, and TRON networks for low fees.
Do I need to set up a crypto wallet?
Yes, you’ll need a wallet to receive payments. NOWPayments provides guides for integrating wallets like MetaMask or Trust Wallet.
What happens if a payment fails?
The stack automatically verifies payments on-chain. If a payment fails, the buyer is prompted to retry. Products are only delivered after payment confirms.
Can I scale this stack as my business grows?
Yes, the Edge Commerce Stack is built on scalable infrastructure. Cloudflare Workers and Supabase can handle high traffic, and you can add more products as needed.
